summary: Ramesh is a dependable L1 agent who gets high ticket counts mostly from auto-routed password, import and how-to cases closed with a stock sentence. He escalates properly with details when needed but has not configured queues or rules. Linux and SQL on his CV are not backed by any work or course effort.

skills.why: Works tickets daily with correct categories and escalation fields; nothing shows queue ownership or assignment-rule changes. Counts are inflated by routed repeats.
Two proper P1/P2 escalations with updates cadence and an ITIL foundation pass; coordinating recovery is done by L2 and L3.
L1 has no server access; no ticket involves a shell. Claim sits only in the CV and HCM self-rating.
A six-minute course tick and no query evidence anywhere.
Course tick of four minutes, no code anywhere.
Only generic communication wording on the CV.

decoys.why: Different ITSM product used at Wipro; no carry over.
Basic network triage at best; no mapped taxonomy skill.

traps.plant: About 1,600 resolved tickets a year, most auto-assigned by rule, with a handful of identical resolution sentences repeated across dozens of records.
LinkedIn Learning SQL and Python courses show completion with 4-6 minutes spent, self-assigned.
CV and HCM list Linux administration; no work record touches it.
Customer-pasted vague short descriptions ('sir kindly check', forwarded mail chains) with category chosen by routing.

answer_behavior.notes: Says yes to level 3 on ServiceNow; says no to Python.
